subclaims.reason: Two concurrent staff GraphQL requests against the same draft order, OrderDiscountAdd.perform_mutation at saleor/graphql/order/mutations/discount_order.py:136-148, OrderDiscountUpdate at saleor/graphql/order/mutations/discount_order.py:186-206, or OrderDiscountDelete at saleor/graphql/order/mutations/discount_order.py:239-247, each run in their own @transaction.atomic DB transaction with no select_for_update on the order or discount rows. Each side reads the order's current total (saleor/order/utils.py:585 in create_order_discount_for_order; saleor/order/utils.py:623 in update_order_discount_for_order; the in-memory order.total at saleor/order/utils.py:648 in remove_order_discount_from_order; or the recompute path in saleor/order/utils.py:142-165 and saleor/graphql/order/mutations/discount_order.py:84-95) and then writes order totals back (saleor/order/utils.py:602, saleor/order/utils.py:157-165, saleor/graphql/order/mutations/discount_order.py:88-95, saleor/order/utils.py:649). The two sides are separated by whole DB statements, SELECT order/discounts then INSERT (saleor/order/utils.py:595) or DELETE (saleor/order/utils.py:646) or UPDATE of the discount then UPDATE of order totals, so a read/read/write/write interleaving loses one side's total adjustment by last-writer-wins: an Add's reduction overwritten by a concurrent Delete or Update computed from the pre-Add total. Postgres read-committed, the configured engine per saleor/settings.py:66-70 with no isolation override and no row locks in these paths, permits this: the SELECTs take no locks so both UPDATEs succeed and the second silently overwrites the first. The switch window spans DB round-trips (socket I/O) that release the GIL, and concurrent requests are normally served by separate threads, processes or workers that share no GIL, so CPython with the GIL can interleave here. Separately, two concurrent Adds both pass the single-discount check at saleor/graphql/order/mutations/discount_order.py:118-127, a plain unlocked SELECT count, and both INSERT, compounding the lost total update.
caveats: Needs two concurrent discount-mutation requests (Add, Update or Delete, or the OrderLine discount mutations that also call recalculate_order) targeting the same draft order, e.g. two staff users or apps racing, or one client racing itself.
Needs concurrently served requests with separate DB connections/transactions (threads, processes or workers); deployment model is UNCONFIRMED.

Needs a DB with read-committed semantics (Postgres, the production engine per saleor/settings.py:66-70); sqlite serializes writers and serializable isolation would abort one side, narrowing or closing the window.
Relies on DB isolation and locking semantics and on the WSGI/task server's concurrency, all outside this tree.
